# PBL-2 EDA numbers (generated by `python src/pbl2_eda.py`; do not edit by hand)

## E01 Density

- 4612 vendors; convex hull area 1399.1 km², i.e. 3.30 vendors per km² on average.

## E02 Clustering tendency

| statistic | vendors | uniform random points |
|---|---|---|
| median NN distance (m) | 44.0 | 257.4 |
| mean NN distance (m) | 105.2 | 275.2 |
| Clark-Evans R = mean NN / CSR expectation | 0.3820 | 0.9994 |
| Hopkins H (mean of 20, m = 300) | 0.9250 (sd 0.0076) | 0.4999 |
| share of vendors with another vendor within 50 m | 0.5353 | 0.0286 |

- R < 1 and H near 1 mean strong clustering, so clustering is meaningful here.
- 53 vendors share exact coordinates with another vendor (same building / mall).

## E03 Neighbours within r

| r (km) | observed | random | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 6.65 | 0.104 | 64.2 |
| 0.25 | 23.37 | 0.647 | 36.1 |
| 0.5 | 57.03 | 2.589 | 22.0 |
| 1.0 | 129.12 | 10.356 | 12.5 |
| 2.0 | 265.61 | 41.425 | 6.4 |
| 5.0 | 607.03 | 258.905 | 2.3 |

- The excess over random is largest at small r and never disappears: clusters exist at street, neighbourhood and town scale. Expect BIC to keep adding components.

## E04 Category co-location

- 223 non-empty 2 km cells. Mean off-diagonal correlation 0.5753 (all positive = busy cells have more of everything; this size effect is why the PCA in section 3 uses shares, not counts).

| category A | category B | corr |
|---|---|---|
| apparel_footwear | stationery_books | 0.764 |
| kirana_provisions | stationery_books | 0.745 |
| hardware | pharmacy | 0.737 |
| apparel_footwear | mobile_accessories | 0.729 |
| fruits | vegetables | 0.725 |
| apparel_footwear | household_homeware | 0.722 |

Weakest pairs:

## E07 First-order structure

- Entropy of a part's symbol ignoring context: 2.943 bits; given the previous part's symbol: 1.902 bits (0.3535 reduction). Knowing the previous part removes a large share of the uncertainty: a first-order Markov assumption captures real structure.
- p(STATEPIN → anything) row sum is 0.0022: the state part is almost always last.
